headline: Toothpick Crisis Leaves Nation on Edge: Dining Etiquette Now a National Emergency
deck: Rationing two toothpicks per meal sparks a diplomatic incident over dinner manners.
article:
In an unprecedented move, the National Bureau of Culinary Standards has declared a state of emergency due to the Great Wooden Toothpick Shortage of 2026. Renowned for its fastidious regulation of dining utensils, the agency has mandated that all citizens limit themselves to just two toothpicks per meal. "We must preserve civility at the dinner table during these trying times," declared Chief Culinary Officer Gladys Timber, her expression a mix of seriousness and disbelief.

As anxiety spreads through suburban dining rooms, local governments are now issuing 'Toothpick Passports.' These coveted documents allow residents to trade in their beloved wooden utensils for dubious government-approved alternatives, including flimsy paper straws that dissolve at the mere thought of a moist hors d'oeuvre. "It’s more about maintaining appearances than actual effectiveness," lamented Harold Puddingstone, a beleaguered city councilman. He added, "We can’t have our food flying all over the place during formal dinners."

In a twist of irony, Reginald Barkley, CEO of Splinterwood Inc., has blamed an aggressive rogue beaver population for the toothpick crisis. In response, the company has initiated a culling program with the catchy motto: "Save Your Toothpicks, Save Your Dinners!" As lumberjacks transition into toothpick hunters, citizens are left grappling with both hunger and etiquette, leading to increasingly absurd interactions at potlucks and bake sales across the nation. In a society more inclined to barter for toothpicks than risk social faux pas, one thing is clear: chaos is looming at the buffet line.
author: Bartholomew Splinter, Senior Culinary Correspondent

oped.title: The Great Toothpick Tyranny: A Plea for Common Sense at the Dinner Table
oped.author: Sir Percy Pompous, Chief Etiquette Enthusiast
oped.body: Ah, the Toothpick Crisis—a scandalous chapter in our otherwise refined dining history! Two toothpicks per meal? Absurd! This farcical rationing reeks of a conspiracy orchestrated by the 'Hat Coalition,' who are undoubtedly envious of our ability to enjoy spaghetti without their ludicrous brims obstructing our view. I propose a daring solution: instead of rationing toothpicks, let’s repurpose those ghastly hats as makeshift utensils! Picture the elegance of plucking pasta with a feathered fedora or skewering shrimp with a stylish sunhat. This way, we thwart the hat-wearers’ plot while preserving our culinary dignity! Remember, it’s not the lack of toothpicks that’s causing this national emergency; it’s the audacity of those who dare to wear hats indoors. We must unite against their tyranny and reclaim our rightful dining decorum—one woolen beret at a time!

Desperately seeking Toothpick Distribution Officer for local tavern. Must possess excellent diplomatic skills and the ability to manage public outrage over 'misplaced' utensils. Pay in free meals—and one extra toothpick for good measure!

Lost: a set of six exquisitely polished toothpicks, last seen at the Broccoli Banquet. Reward offered in maple syrup or vintage wooden dolls. Please return; my dinner guests are currently staging a protest!

In light of the Toothpick Crisis, all citizens are hereby advised to check toothpick stock before hosting any meals. Any breach of etiquette will result in mandatory workshops hosted by the National Fork Association. Attendance is non-negotiable!

stories.headline: Local HOA Bans Dining Outside as Toothpick Shortage Escalates
stories.deck: Neighbors fear that toothpick-free picnics could lead to lawn chaos.
stories.article:
In a surprising twist, the Maplewood Heights Homeowners Association has imposed an emergency ban on outdoor dining, citing concerns that unregulated picnicking could result in toothpick-related pandemonium. The HOA has established strict penalties for anyone caught enjoying a sandwich without adhering to the two-toothpick limit, as rogue stacks of finger foods might threaten neighborhood stability.

Residents have begun crafting elaborate disguises for their illicit outdoor meals, including hollowed-out wooden dining tables and custom-designed wax paper tents. Meanwhile, local squirrels have seized the opportunity, launching a thriving black-market toothpick operation from the park's underbrush.

stories.headline: Wooden Toy Theft Ring Exposed After Failed Heist
stories.deck: Suspects believed to be driven by a desperate need for hobby-grade marbles.
stories.article:
Authorities in Riverton have apprehended a gang of thieves attempting to make off with an entire shipment of handcrafted wooden toys from a local warehouse. The heist collapsed when the gang discovered their getaway vehicle—a converted tin toy car—was too small to accommodate more than two blocks of the coveted merchandise.

While the gang is suspected of targeting limited-edition marbles made from glass, local children are breathing a sigh of relief that their supply of meticulously carved action figures remains safe. Investigators are still scratching their heads over how the thieves thought they could escape in a vehicle that wouldn’t even fit a rubber duck.
